contract.review_scope: Complete captured body structure and stated guarded control values; opaque selector labels, callers and operational acceptance remain bounded gaps.
contract.purpose: Split a shipping-container quantity, optionally creating a parent container.
inputs_defaults: qty numeric(19,5), internalContNum numeric(9), userName nvarchar(30), newInternalContNum numeric(9) OUTPUT, newParentContNum numeric(9) OUTPUT, all required; no defaults.
null_and_invalid_input_behavior: Missing source is not explicitly rejected; zero-row clone is not a checked failure. qty exceeding source skips original reduction but can create an oversized clone. Zero quantity can divide by zero. newParentContNum is unchanged when parent branch is skipped; early returns do not clear outputs.
output_shape: New child ID via SCOPE_IDENTITY; parent output assigned only when parent-creation branch runs. Explicit -1 for selected invalid inputs/checked SQL errors.

ordered_branches.explanation: Reject NULL/nonpositive ID or qty. If source has container ID and item and is not the fixed detail-container type, clone it as a new parent.

Clear parent item, line, quantity, location/work/lot/allocation fields and set WORK_CREATED to the captured negative flag. Convert original to a detail child, clearing its own ID, manifest/tracking/freight/return/container-count data while linking it to the new parent.
Clone the current original into a new shipping-container row and capture identity.
Reduce original quantity by requested qty only when original quantity is at least qty; proportionally scale weight, volume and value.
Set clone quantity to requested qty and proportionally scale its weight, volume and value without the same upper-bound guard; stamp final updates.

contract.status_and_quantity_effects: Only the explicitly described persistent writes occur in this body.
configuration_scope_and_precedence: The supplied selectors govern this body. No separate effective setting or cross-layer precedence is established; configuration values were not queried.
error_and_return_handling: Checks @@ERROR after INSERTs and final proportional UPDATEs; several intermediate parent/child UPDATEs have no immediate explicit error check. No custom catch, rollback or row-count guarantee.
contract.transaction_ownership: No explicit BEGIN/COMMIT/ROLLBACK transaction, savepoint, TRY/CATCH or XACT_ABORT is introduced. Caller/session transaction semantics govern effects.
concurrency: Persistent statements are not collectively protected by a body-owned transaction. Concurrent changes between reads and writes can alter selected state; no application retry or idempotency guarantee is present.
contract.trigger_behavior: INSERT into SHIPPING_CONTAINER can invoke the captured ship_container_tree_unit_a_i trigger that initializes parentless TREE_UNIT; exact transactional composition and all table constraints remain caller/schema concerns.
external_handoffs_and_gaps: No inventory movement, work creation, allocation-request split, status authorization or complete child-tree reconciliation is performed here. Caller quantity validation and transaction ownership are required for safe composition.

NO_CAPTURED_REFERENCE means none of the credited channels in this exact retained corpus identified the table. It does not establish that the table is unused, obsolete, a backup, safe to delete, or absent from external application SQL.
Dynamic SQL, runtime-selected identifiers, external callers, client-generated SQL, uncaptured jobs and historical/other database code can use tables without a resolvable reference here.

The bounded lexer recognizes named SQL relation/DML positions and local aliases/CTEs; it is not the SQL Server binder. Unqualified names assume a unique captured name, not verified caller/default-schema resolution. Unsupported or ambiguous syntax remains explicit.
